InnoTek acquires 60% stake in Ablewin Technology Sdn Bhd for RM20.3 mil
article:
InnoTek Limited announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, InnoTek Holding (S) Pte Ltd, has entered into a joint venture agreement with Taiwan-based Ablecom Technology through the acquisition of a 60% stake in Ablewin Technology Sdn Bhd for a total consideration of RM20.3 million ($6.3 million).

The remaining 40% stake is held by Ablecom Technology, which is a global provider of high-end server chassis, advanced modular racks and liquid cooling solutions engineered for AI and high-performance computing.

Through this joint venture, InnoTek will offer sheet metal processing, stamping and assembly services for components related to GPU and non-GPU server chassis, server racks, liquid cooling systems, and industrial power supplies, among others.

Besides manufacturing components for Ablecom, both parties will cooperate in terms of securing projects from new customers.

“Having served Ablecom as our customer for several years, we are pleased to deepen our relationship through the joint venture,” says Lou Yiliang, InnoTek’s CEO.

“With Ablewin Technology based in Malaysia, we gain a strategically located production base to better serve the growing demand for AI server infrastructure across the region,” adds Steve Liang, Ablecom’s chairman.

Shares of Innotek closed 3.5 cents higher, or up 10.3% at 37.5 cents on Nov 25.

title: Arnault can lead family’s LVMH holding company until he’s 95
article:
(Nov 25): Bernard Arnault, the 77-year-old chief executive officer and chairman of LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE, can lead the family holding company which controls the luxury goods conglomerate for another 18 years.

The billionaire will be able to stay until the age of 95 as managing general partner of Agache SCA, according to a filing this week issued as part of a previously announced plan to tighten the family’s grip on LVMH.

The strategy includes merging Agache with another LVMH holding company Christian Dior SE, whose shareholders are due to meet at the end of December to approve the transaction. The age cap of 95 for Arnault is 10 years older than the current limit for his chairman role at Christian Dior SE, and for the CEO position held by his 49-year-old son, Antoine.

Following the merger, almost all of the Arnault family’s stake in the group would be held in the single listed entity, Agache.

The limited joint-stock partnership will hold a direct stake in LVMH of 49.76% of the share capital and 65.55% of the voting rights after the latest changes are approved, it said in September.

Known as a société en commandite par actions, the structure is used by families to cement their grip over a group — legal experts call it a “padlock.”

See also: HSBC plans SRTs tied to US$7 bil of US, Asian corporate loans — Bloomberg

Arnault has an estimated net worth of about US$130 billion ($167.9 billion), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. He has five children who all work inside LVMH.

The French businessman has previously joked after lifting the age cap of the CEO role at LVMH to 80 from 75 that Warren Buffett — who is 19 years older than Arnault — had asked him why he hadn’t pushed the limit higher. Buffett, who’s 96, stepped down as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway Inc last year.

The age limit of the CEO role Arnault holds at LVMH is now 85.
